We need to return the mapped_rxn associated with the template that, when applied to the molecule (c1ccc(cc1)Br), reproduces the electrophilic bromination of an aromatic ring (substituting H with Br). This is a retrosynthetic step: target is bromobenzene (aryl bromide). The retrosynthetic step would break the C-Br bond to give benzene (or phenyl) plus Br? Actually forward reaction: benzene + Br2 -> bromobenzene + HBr. Retrosynthesis: bromobenzene -> benzene + Br (or HBr). The template should replace Br with H (i.e., remove Br). The template that when applied to bromobenzene yields benzene (or phenyl) as precursor. In the search results, many templates produce bromobenzene from something else. We need the template that when applied to the molecule reproduces the reaction (i.e., forward). But we are doing retrosynthetic step, so we need a template that when applied to the target (bromobenzene) gives precursors (benzene + Br?). The earlier "make_8_lvl2-apply_template-3" answer was [] meaning applying some template gave no precursors. We need to find the correct template.

Look at result entry 1141: retro_smarts_template: '[Br;H0;D1;+0:1]-[c;H0;D3;+0:3](:[c:2]):[c:4]>>Br-[Br;H0;D1;+0:1].[c:2]:[cH;D2;+0:3]:[c:4]'. This is a retrosynthetic template that breaks C-Br bond to give Br-Br (bromine) and aromatic with H. Applying to bromobenzene should give Br-Br (i.e., Br2) and benzene. The mapped_rxn shows Br[Br:5].Br.[CH3:1][C:2]1=... That's for a methyl-substituted ring, not plain benzene. But still could work.

We need to test which template matches the molecule. Use check_smiles_reaction_template_matching for each candidate. Let's try template_id 1141.
